draft.title: Observational learning
card: Observational learning is learning by watching a model, a person whose behaviour is copied. The learner does not need to do the behaviour first or be rewarded for it.
Bandura's model has five steps. Attention: the learner notices the model. Retention: the learner stores what they saw in memory.
Reproduction: the learner is able to carry out the behaviour. Motivation: the learner has a reason to do it, such as seeing the model rewarded.
Reinforcement: after the learner tries the behaviour, a good result makes them more likely to do it again. A learner can pay attention and remember, but still not copy the behaviour.
draft.remember: Watch, remember, be able, want to, then be reinforced.

a.q: Jai watches his coach demonstrate a swimming turn and can describe each movement a week later. Which step does this show?
opts: Retention, as he stored what he saw in memory
Attention, as he noticed the coach's turn
Reproduction, as he can carry out the turn
Motivation, as he has a reason to copy the turn
a.why: Describing the movements a week later shows he stored them in memory, which is retention. Attention is the tempting answer, but it is only noticing the model. Remembering later goes beyond noticing.
a.clue: Which step is about storing what was seen?

b.q: Lena watches her older cousin bake bread and remembers every step. She has the skills to bake, but she does not try because she saw no reason to. Which step is missing?
opts: Motivation
Attention
Retention
Reproduction
b.why: Lena noticed the model, remembered the steps and has the skill, so attention, retention and reproduction are all in place. She has no reason to copy the behaviour, so motivation is missing. Reproduction is tempting, but it is about being able to do the behaviour, and she is able.
b.clue: She can do it. What is stopping her from wanting to?

a.best: Retention, as he stored what he saw in memory

problems.detail: The clue ('What is stopping her from wanting to?') names the missing step outright, since the card and remember line define motivation as 'want to'. The stem also says she 'saw no reason to', which echoes the card's 'has a reason to do it'. A student can match words without applying the idea.
The clue ('Which step is about storing what was seen?') repeats the card's definition of retention almost word for word, and that wording appears only in the right option. This hands over the answer.
